title: Impact of Mygalin on Inflammatory Response Induced by Toll-like Receptor 2 Agonists and IFN-gamma Activation.
authors: Del Santos, Nayara; Vazquez-Ramirez, Ricardo; Mendes, Elizabeth; Silva Junior, Pedro Ismael; Borges, Monamaris Marques
one_liner_zh: 该文研究蜘蛛来源合成分子Mygalin对TLR2激动剂诱导炎症的抑制，涉及分子对接分析Mygalin与TLR2/1、TLR2/6复合物的相互作用，但对象为蛋白-小分子而非蛋白-DNA互作，且无TF-DNA结合建模，仅方法可部分借鉴。
abstract: Several natural products are being studied to identify new bioactive molecules with therapeutic potential for infections, immune modulation, and other pathologies. TLRs are a family of receptors that play a crucial role in the immune system, constituting the first line of immune defense. They recognize specific products derived from microorganisms that activate multiple pathways and transcription factors in target cells, which are vital for producing immune mediators. Mygalin is a synthetic acylpolyamine derived from hemocytes of the spider Acanthoscurria gomesiana. This molecule negatively regulates macrophage response to LPS stimulation by interacting with MD2 in the TLR4/MD2 complex. Here, we investigated the activity of Mygalin mediated by TLR2 agonists in cells treated with Pam3CSK4 (TLR2/1), Pam2CSK4, Zymosan (TLR2/6), and IFN-gamma. Our data showed that Mygalin significantly inhibited stimulation with agonists and IFN-gamma, reducing NO and IL-6 synthesis, regardless of the stimulation. There was also a significant reduction in the phosphorylation of proteins NF-kappaB p65 and STAT-1 in cells treated with Pam3CSK4. Molecular docking assays determined the molecular structure of Mygalin and agonists Pam3CSK4, Pam2CSK4, and Zymosan, as well as their interaction and free energy with the heterodimeric complexes TLR2/1 and TLR2/6. Mygalin interacted with the TLR1 and TLR2 dimer pathway through direct interaction with the agonists, and the ligand-binding domain was similar in both complexes. However, the binding of Mygalin was different from that of the agonists, since the interaction energy with the receptors was lower than with the agonists for their receptors. In conclusion, this study showed the great potential of Mygalin as a potent natural inhibitor of TLR2/1 and TLR2/6 and a suppressor of the inflammatory response induced by TLR2 agonists, in part due to its ability to interact with the heterodimeric complexes.
abstract_zh: 目前正在研究几种天然产物，以鉴定具有治疗感染、免疫调节及其他病理状况潜力的新型生物活性分子。TLRs是一类在免疫系统中发挥关键作用的受体家族，构成免疫防御的第一道防线。它们识别源自微生物的特异性产物，这些产物激活靶细胞中的多种通路和转录因子，对产生免疫介质至关重要。Mygalin是一种合成酰基多胺，来源于蜘蛛Acanthoscurria gomesiana的血细胞。该分子通过与TLR4/MD2复合物中的MD2相互作用，负向调节巨噬细胞对LPS刺激的反应。在此，我们研究了Mygalin在经Pam3CSK4 (TLR2/1)、Pam2CSK4、Zymosan (TLR2/6)及IFN-gamma处理的细胞中由TLR2激动剂介导的活性。我们的数据表明，Mygalin显著抑制了激动剂和IFN-gamma的刺激，无论刺激类型如何，均减少了NO和IL-6的合成。在Pam3CSK4处理的细胞中，NF-kappaB p65和STAT-1蛋白的磷酸化也显著降低。分子对接实验确定了Mygalin及激动剂Pam3CSK4、Pam2CSK4和Zymosan的分子结构，以及它们与异二聚体复合物TLR2/1和TLR2/6的相互作用和自由能。Mygalin通过与激动剂直接相互作用，与TLR1和TLR2二聚体通路结合，且两个复合物中的配体结合域相似。然而，Mygalin的结合方式与激动剂不同，因为其与受体的相互作用能低于激动剂与其受体的相互作用能。总之，本研究展示了Mygalin作为TLR2/1和TLR2/6强效天然抑制剂及TLR2激动剂诱导炎症反应抑制剂的巨大潜力，部分归因于其与异二聚体复合物相互作用的能力。
